prize_parts.citation: For introducing firm heterogeneity and selection into exporting and foreign investment, and thereby reshaping the theory and empirics of the gains from trade.

statement.case_for: Firm heterogeneity with selection into exporting (Melitz 2003; Helpman-Melitz-Yeaple 2004) is a conceptual reorganisation of international trade. It moved the unit of analysis from the industry to the firm and added a reallocation and productivity-selection channel for the gains from trade. It also gave a theory to which the firm-level micro-data work could be tied, and it is now standard in graduate teaching, structural work and policy evaluation, with reach into macro, growth and development. The attribution is comparatively tight: Melitz is the originator of the core model, and Helpman supplies the exports-versus-FDI margin and the broader monopolistic-competition foundations. The core papers are more than twenty years old and have been tested repeatedly in firm data across many countries. After the discussion I still rank this first. The colleagues' arguments I find strongest concern the attribution boundary, not the merit of the discovery, and I address them below.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is attribution. Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum made closely related empirical and quantitative contributions that are not credited on this ballot entry, and a two-person award could be read as under-crediting a wider lineage. Redding's quantitative and spatial work is a credited name that I leave out. The baseline Melitz model's welfare results depend on functional-form assumptions, and some of its predictions are rejected in detail, although the literature has extended it rather than abandoned it. Helpman's wider body of work, including the political economy of protection and the possible pairing with Grossman in B047, could also support a different trade framing. Finally, trade is a field in which a further award would need to be weighed against how the Committee frames the earlier 2008 recognition.

responses.point: Hassler ranks the BLP demand-estimation and dynamic-oligopoly work (B006) first. He argues that it is fully mature, cleanly attributable to Berry, Levinsohn and Pakes, and that it is the working toolkit of merger review, antitrust and empirical IO well beyond its home subfield.
responses.response: I agree that B006 has a strong claim on maturity, breadth of use and attribution, and I did not rank it in my opening eight, so I take the comparison seriously. My preference for B001 is not that B006 is weak. Methodological reach and a change in how a field thinks are different kinds of contribution, and I judge that the heterogeneous-firm framework changed both the conceptual content of trade theory and its empirical agenda, while B006 changed mainly the empirical toolkit. I also see more boundary ambiguity in B006, between the demand-estimation strand and the dynamic-games strand and in the Bresnahan, Reiss, Benkard and Levin names, than in the two-name core of B001. The gap is modest, and I would not defend it as a scientific ordering independent of how the Committee weighs tool-building against conceptual advance.

responses.point: Boppart agrees that Melitz is the central model but flags that Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum are important parallel contributors outside the credited set. He also notes that Krugman's earlier prize covered part of the new-trade-theory lineage.
responses.response: The omission of Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum is a real attribution risk, but it is a constraint of the ballot entry: those names cannot be credited in this configuration, and I do not think it should be resolved by stretching the credited set. I would handle it through the citation. It is worded around the theoretical framework of firm heterogeneity and selection into exporting and investment, and it does not claim the empirical facts on exporter premia or the quantitative Eaton-Kortum tradition. On Krugman, I read the 2008 recognition as covering scale economies and intra-industry trade. Selection across heterogeneous firms is a distinct step, not a duplicate of that prize, and the 2008 date also means trade has been absent for nearly two decades.

responses.point: Friberg ranks B001 first but stresses that the three-person limit forces a hard choice. He asks whether Redding, or Bernard, Eaton and Kortum, should be credited alongside or instead of the proposed pair, and whether a quantitative-trade framing (B037) or a broader trade prize including B047 would be preferable.
responses.response: I would keep Redding out. His quantitative and spatial work is substantial, but it builds on the heterogeneous-firm and gravity foundations and is not the origin of the selection discovery named in this entry. Friberg is right that this exclusion becomes less comfortable if the Committee defines the discovery more broadly, as the gains from trade with quantification, and in that case Redding's claim would rise. I would then prefer to examine that as a separate framing and not enlarge this one. On B047, I do not think pairing Helpman there rather than here is a reason to prefer it. It is a different discovery, and the Committee should compare the two directly if it sees them as competing uses of Helpman, not assume one displaces the other.

uncertainties: Whether the Committee would prefer to define the discovery more broadly, for example including the quantitative-trade lineage (B037) or pairing Helpman with Grossman (B047), and how that would change the credited names.
How much weight the omission of Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum, who are not on the ballot entry, should carry in the attribution.
Whether Redding's quantitative and spatial contributions merit inclusion if the discovery is framed more broadly.
How to compare a conceptual reorganisation of a field (B001) with the broadest methodological-reach candidate (B006) when the scientific gap is modest.
My assessment rests on general knowledge as presented in the supplied openings, and I have not independently verified citations or priority records.
statement.conflict_note: None apparent from the supplied profile with Helpman or Melitz. My profile lists SSE affiliation shared with committee colleagues Dreber Almenberg, Friberg and Strömberg, and none of my listed co-authors or networks is connected to the proposed laureates. I disclose this without adjudicating it.
